doc.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021

title: Pandemic life, Spain and the lockdown album
summary: He splits time between New York and Barcelona, makes online videos, released a lockdown-recorded Arbors album and livestreamed a seven-piece CD release.

bands.name: Professor Cunningham and his Old School

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Okay, so since then, since a year has passed now, have you had to find ways to do other things now that gigs are almost nonexistent?

It’s been pretty brutal. I’ve been actually dividing my time between New York and Spain. So my girlfriend lives in Barcelona. And I met her three years ago because I’d been doing so much touring in my band, we’ve been on the road so much, we ended up spending a

lot of time in Spain. We had a good following in Spain so I met a lovely girl in Barcelona and we thought where is this going to go. But then we continued to see each other and it developed into something really good so in the last — since last summer I’ve kind of been dividing my time 50/50 between here and there. Essentially I need my time in America to keep my green card. So my days here, to keep my residency, because there’s still very little work, and there’s even less in Barcelona actually. But I think, there has been opportunities to do a lot of online stuff, you know, I’ve been putting together videos for festivals, you know you’ve probably been involved in some of that yourself, you know where you have to be videos together, online concerts, things like that. So that’s at least something. And my New Orleans band, Professor Cunningham, we released an album through Arbors, well it came out last December. It was recorded all in lockdown, from our own private rooms. And we put it all together. That was quite a project, yeah. A lot of work.
And you probably haven’t had a chance to actually recreate those tunes in a live setting.
Well we actually livestreamed a CD release last Friday.

Just the other night. The full 7-piece band. It’s the first time the band has played live like that since, what February last year. So that was really nice to hear the music, actual, in a room together you know. And it works thank God. But yeah, I mean to play with a full band, we were all just saying to each other my God it’s so loud all these musicians together. We’d forgotten how loud it is. It’s like holy shit this is like a lot of noise in this room.
